# Account Intelligence Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Account Intelligence Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 22 captured build checkpoints; 6 skills; 2 knowledge files; 6 acceptance checks; 6 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment, publisher prefix and maker access. Confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model; keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review policies for uploaded account files, proposed seller-data sources and the intended channel; document blocked paths rather than bypass them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always trigger; record who may build, test and use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for Dynamics 365 Sales, SharePoint, Microsoft Teams and any business-intelligence source. No customer connection is needed for the workshop. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare account-executive, sales-director, customer-success and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; do not publish the workshop to share it. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio browser and reviewed files. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Account evidence ownership | The account owner approves replacement account, contact and competitor sources; keep live customer data out of the synthetic workshop knowledge. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales leadership

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Account-preparation sources and coverage gaps before customer meetings. Preparation is spread across records, relationship history, news, competitor notes and seller memory; agree success measures before building.

Fill your baseline record:

| Account | Measurement period | Preparation sources used | Stakeholder coverage gaps | Preparation owner | Review route |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree seller-workflow replacement connections, governance, support, telemetry and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales leadership

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Sales leadership | Approve seller-facing scope, production seams and success measures; never treat synthetic scores or projections as customer results. |
| Authorized account owner | Validate account facts, stakeholder roles, messaging, references, risks and next steps before any customer-facing use. |
| Legal, privacy and commercial reviewers | Review contact data, claims, references and pricing positions where relevant; retain decisions the draft skills must not make. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and six skills; remove web search, add no tools and record the owned agent's Draft state. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any seller-data connection is approved. |
| Account data connection owners | Approve Dynamics 365 Sales, SharePoint, Microsoft Teams and business-intelligence access with dedicated references; own connection failures. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check AI-01 through AI-06, the boundary tests and Easy/Manual parity; reject reshoot-required frames and uncited answers. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route account decisions to the account owner. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Planned seller-workflow replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures are agreed.
- [ ] The sales owner records where account preparation is spread today before choosing customer success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/account-intelligence/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and publisher prefix are approved and recorded before any build starts.
- [ ] The customer approves the authenticated seller audience and least-privilege scopes for account and contact data.
- [ ] The environment's data policies for knowledge sources, connectors, skills and channels are approved.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/account-intelligence/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/account-intelligence/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/account-intelligence/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/account-intelligence/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Account Intelligence Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_account-intelligence-operating-rules.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_account-intelligence-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: account-overview
9. Add skill: competitive-intel
10. Add skill: executive-briefing
11. Add skill: risk-assessment
12. Add skill: stakeholder-map
13. Add skill: value-messaging
14. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
15. Open a fresh Preview conversation
16. Pass AI-01: Account Executive
17. Pass AI-02: Account Executive
18. Pass AI-03: Sales Director
19. Pass AI-04: Account Executive
20. Pass AI-05: Sales Director
21. Pass AI-06: Customer Success Manager
22. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: AI-01, AI-02, AI-03, AI-04, AI-05, AI-06. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, model, inventory and Draft state.
- [ ] If this lane is chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `AccountIntelligenceAgent` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, six skills and the confirmed model; web search is removed and no tools exist.
- [ ] Unchanged locked prompts pass in separate fresh Preview chats on the owned Draft.
- [ ] The deterministic validator judges each full final response; an annotated image is only a learner checkpoint.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before accessing account and contact information. Request only the scopes necessary for approved account sources. Restrict the seller audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365 Sales

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Account data connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 Sales — read:** Bind scoped read-only connector or API actions.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 Sales:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 Sales:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 Sales:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 6](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): State that the fixed snapshot does not contain that account; never substitute Acme or invent records. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a live lookup, CRM change or sent message succeeded.

### Step 3-2. Integrate SharePoint

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Account data connection owners

1. **Bind SharePoint — read:** Add approved SharePoint knowledge with a content owner.

2. **Identity for SharePoint:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope SharePoint:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for SharePoint:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 6](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): State that the fixed snapshot does not contain that account; never substitute Acme or invent records. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): State that it is absent; do not browse, enrich or substitute another account.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Microsoft Teams

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Account data connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams — read-write:** Start read-only; gate any message, meeting or task workflow behind approval (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Return drafts marked for human review; never report a message as sent. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a live lookup, CRM change or sent message succeeded.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Approved business-intelligence source

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Account data connection owners

1. **Bind Approved business-intelligence source — read:** Use a dedicated approved connection reference and read-only actions.

2. **Identity for Approved business-intelligence source:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved business-intelligence source:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved business-intelligence source:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 6](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): State that the fixed snapshot does not contain that account; never substitute Acme or invent records. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a live lookup, CRM change or sent message succeeded.

### Step 3-5. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Account data connection owners

Create dedicated connection references for the approved seams only and validate each binding.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Each wired seam uses a dedicated reference for an approved production connection, never an ambiguous existing one.
- [ ] No live lookup, CRM change or sent message is claimed unless an approved tool returns success evidence.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Run adapted evaluations under an approved authenticated test profile so the agent's tools and connections are fully testable.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The sales owner sets acceptance thresholds on customer data; synthetic scores, indicators and projections are not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; exact assertions stay separate from General quality scoring.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked account corpus | All six cases, AI-01 through AI-06, satisfy every required and forbidden marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, six skills and the reviewed model; web search removed and no tools. |
| Read-only seller boundary | Any CRM write, task, meeting, message, outreach, proposal, pricing approval or forecast change is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Reuse only frames showing a positive expected-state anchor without a blocker; withhold reshoot-required frames. |
| Release state | The owned workshop agent is Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales leadership

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sales leadership

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved seller audience and channels are selected, and the agent is tested in Preview before publication.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review seller session transcripts, failed turns, tool authentication errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Pull before editing, push reviewed changes, then package the workspace with `pac copilot pack` for solution import.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, retrieval gaps, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.
